title: Reverse Mortgages Explained in Plain Words
bigPicture: A reverse mortgage lets homeowners 62 and older borrow against their home equity with no regular monthly mortgage payment, but interest and fees keep adding to what is owed.
whatYouNeedToKnow: A reverse mortgage is a loan, most often a Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM), that lets you borrow against your home's equity.
You keep ownership of the home and make no regular monthly mortgage payment.
The home must be your principal residence. You must keep paying property taxes and homeowners insurance and maintain the home.
Lenders add interest and fees to the loan balance each month, so the amount you owe rises over time while your home equity shrinks.
Repayment is triggered once you no longer live in the home. You or your heirs must eventually repay, usually by selling the home.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Forgetting that interest and fees grow the balance every month.
Falling behind on property taxes, insurance, or upkeep, which you are still responsible for.
Not telling your family. Your heirs will need to repay the loan, usually by selling the home.
actionSteps: Ask each lender for all fees and the interest rate in writing before you decide.
Talk it over with your family and with a trusted, independent advisor.
Read the CFPB page below before you sign anything.
